approach: Recognize the spring balance sits inline with one continuous string over two pulleys joining unequal masses, so it reads the standard Atwood tension, not either weight alone.

steps.text: One continuous string runs from the 5 kg mass, over the left pulley, through the spring balance, over the right pulley, to the 10 kg mass, so the balance reads the tension that string carries throughout.
The pulleys only redirect the string; since 10 kg ≠ 5 kg the masses are free to accelerate, so this is an Atwood pair and the reading is the standard Atwood tension.
Substitute m₁ = 5 kg, m₂ = 10 kg, g = 10 m/s² (the value that makes the given options come out as round numbers).
Compare this with the printed options 50 N, 100 N and 150 N — it matches none of them.

common_mistakes.text: Assuming the balance directly reads the heavier hanging weight, 10 kg × 10 m/s² = 100 N, without accounting for the system's acceleration.
Assuming the balance reads the combined weight of both masses as if the system were static, (5+10) kg × 10 m/s² = 150 N.
